Confirmed. And good news — your `.gitattributes` already uses exactly this pattern (`*CHANGELOG.md merge=union`, commented "so upstream syncs never hard-conflict"). So the fix slots right into an established fork convention.

There are two *independent* problems with two independent fixes:

## The fix

**Lever 1 — kill the dirty-tree-after-build** (the daily annoyance)
Decouple generation from `build`. In `packages/ai/package.json`:
```
"build":           "tsgo -p tsconfig.build.json"          // was: generate-models && generate-image-models && tsgo
"refresh-models":  "npm run generate-models && npm run generate-image-models"
```
The committed snapshot is ordinary TS — it compiles/tests/runs fine without regenerating. So `build:binary` stops re-fetching live registries → **clean tree after every rebuild.** New model data appears only when *you* run `npm run refresh-models` deliberately.

**Lever 2 — kill the merge conflict on upstream sync**
Append to `.gitattributes`:
```
packages/ai/src/models.generated.ts        merge=ours
packages/ai/src/image-models.generated.ts  merge=ours
```
`merge=ours` makes upstream's churn in those files auto-resolve to *your* version (no conflict). Needs the driver registered once: `git config merge.ours.driver true` — local config, so I'd add a tiny checked-in `scripts/setup-merge-drivers.sh` + a line in the sync runbook so it survives fresh clones.

**Skipping a `--check` gate on purpose:** the data is live/non-deterministic, so a strict check would flake every time a registry tweaks a number. Not worth it.

**Net behavior:** builds never dirty the tree; syncs never conflict on these files; you refresh model data when you choose, getting fresh-on-demand live values instead of upstream's stale-by-merge-time snapshot. Trade-off: the committed snapshot goes stale between manual refreshes — acceptable, since refresh re-fetches everything live anyway.

This is a build-pipeline + merge-policy divergence on the core fork → I'd log it in `FORK-CHANGELOG.md` + `my-pi/docs/pi-fork-patch-inventory.md`, and it's ADR-worthy.
